title: STILL PRESENT (r1): W3 wrong fix — corrected_at staleness gate is a format-mixed lexical compare; same-day stale pre-correction bounces still exhaust the corrected row
detail: matched_send_at is RFC3339 ('2026-08-11T09:00:00Z'); corrected_at is timestamptz::text ('2026-08-11 10:30:00+00'). Same calendar date → char 10 'T'(0x54) > ' '(0x20), so any pre-correction same-day send compares NEWER than the correction → genuine_failure=true → exhaust_row terminalizes the row and stamps referee_contact_invalid on a contact never re-tried (the exact W3 harm).
recommended_fix: Compare in one canonical format in SQL: (e->>'at')::timestamptz < rc.corrected_at, or emit corrected_at via to_char(...,'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') so the lexical compare is truly chronological.

title: STILL PRESENT (r1): N10 — substitute_reference_call.sql still duplicates the live-slot ON CONFLICT predicate instead of reusing the canonical insert (now 4 maintenance sites)
evidence: substitute_reference_call.sql:37: "ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (" ; substitute_reference_call.sql:51: "AND rc.status NOT IN (" ; insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql:28: "ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (" ; migration:140: "WHERE status NOT IN ('form_completed','unreachable','refused','objected','manual_recorded','failed','completed','partial');"
detail: The substitute CTE carries its own copies of the live-slot predicate (ON CONFLICT + existing SELECT) rather than reusing insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql; the predicate now lives in 4 places (migration index, insert file, substitute x2). All identical today, but the drift risk is unchanged from r1.
recommended_fix: Extract the predicate into one shared constant in sql.gleam referenced by both inserts, and pin a test asserting all copies match — removes the 4-way maintenance burden.

title: W6 re-arm is inert and app-wide: every transition into 'queued' already sets next_attempt_at = now(), so rearm_queued_reference_calls cannot change delivery timing; a ?slot= per-row start re-arms sibling rows too
evidence: trigger.gleam:532 (inside run_start_action, shared by the whole-app AND slot-filtered starts): "case sql.rearm_queued_reference_calls(config.db, app_uuid) {" ; rearm_queued_reference_calls.sql: "UPDATE reference_call SET next_attempt_at = now(), updated_at = now() WHERE application_id = $1 AND status = 'queued'::reference_call_status AND taken_over_at IS NULL" ; every path into queued stamps now(): insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql ("next_attempt_at"), correct_reference_call.sql:35 ("next_attempt_at = now()"), re_enable_reference_call.sql ("next_attempt_at = now()")
detail: Queued rows are always already due, so the re-arm is a no-op and the §7.4 'sends the invite now' promise still waits for the next sweep tick; and on a per-row ?slot= start the app-wide re-arm touches sibling rows (inert today, wrong scoping).
recommended_fix: Scope the re-arm to the requested slot (add a ref_slot parameter, run it only when slot_filter is None), or drop it and instead trigger a targeted sweep tick for the row if 'now' is genuinely promised.
